title: Point Roberts, the US Town You Drive to via Canada #shorts
summary: The 1846 Oregon Treaty ran the border along the 49th parallel and left Point Roberts, Washington (1,191 people in 2020) reachable by road only through British Columbia.
sources: Oregon Treaty, 15 Jun 1846, Article I: the line continues westward along the 49th parallel to the middle of the channel separating the continent from Vancouver's Island (Avalon Project, Yale Law School): https://avalon.law.yale.edu/19th_century/br-1846.asp

HistoryLink.org Essay 9158, Point Roberts -- Thumbnail History (Phil Dougherty, 2009): a 4.9-square-mile unincorporated American exclave; under the 1846 Oregon Treaty the lower Tsawwassen Peninsula dipped into the US; a 14-mile boat trip from Blaine or a drive nearly twice that far through Canada; the grade school closed in 1963 and students were bused to Blaine, more than 25 miles away; the population more than triples in summer: https://www.historylink.org/file/9158

US Census Bureau, 2020 Census via TIGERweb: Point Roberts CDP, WA: population 1,191, housing units 2,175, land 12,652,612 m2 (about 4.9 sq mi): https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/tigerWMS_Census2020/MapServer/28/query?where=GEOID%3D%275355015%27&outFields=NAME,GEOID,POP100,HU100,AREALAND,AREAWATER&returnGeometry=false&f=json

Map data: Natural Earth (public domain) https://www.naturalearthdata.com and US Census Bureau cartographic boundary files (public domain) https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/carto-boundary-file.html; drive and boat routes are drawn schematically

scenes.narration: This is Point Roberts, Washington: the tip of a peninsula south of Vancouver.
In {1846|eighteen forty-six}, the Oregon Treaty ran the border along the {49th parallel|forty-ninth parallel}.
In {2020|twenty twenty}, {1,191|eleven hundred and ninety-one} people lived there.
By boat, the US mainland is {14 miles|fourteen miles} away. By road, more than {25|twenty-five}.
Every drive to the mainland crosses the border twice: into Canada, and back out.
